summary: Erratic 5xx elevation during variant reshuffle causing bursty runtime crashes and API gateway saturation
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC a subset of requests routed to Acme AI's dedicated pool began returning elevated 5xx rates (502/503) clustered in short waves. Impact: customer-facing endpoints experienced ~18% error rate for 3-8 minute bursts, disrupting live chat sessions and inference throughput for Acme AI's production tenants. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1 serving pinned model 'gpt-medium-v1' with recent variant reshuffle rolled out at 02:05 UTC. Observed behavior: apigw queues grow, large number of half-closed HTTP/2 streams, runtime processes crash with NVML/GPU driver timeouts during ephemeral-worker thaw. This ticket tracks triage, mitigation, and root cause investigation.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy variant reshuffle: shift 20% of traffic to newer variant of gpt-medium-v1 using canary rollout policy
2) Simulate production traffic burst (sustained 150 qps with single-token prompts and multiplexed streaming connections),
3) Observe API gateway accept queue latency and increase in 502/503 responses within ~2-5 minutes after rollout start
4) Check runtime nodes for NVML timeout logs and repeated watchdog restarts
logs: [runtime-logs] 2026-03-12T02:12:18Z ERROR nvml: GPU reset timeout after 120s, killing process pid=22458
[sre] 2026-03-12T02:14:05Z INFO mitigation: pinned route to previous variant for Acme AI tenant; in-flight requests draining
investigation: Initial hypothesis: variant reshuffle changed sequence length distribution and led to sudden KV-cache warmups combined with ephemeral-worker thaw, which increased GPU kernel compilation/IO and triggered NVML timeouts.
Dashboard review: token-per-request distribution shifted to longer tail on canary variant; per-token latency for gpt-medium-v1-canary spiked 3x compared to baseline.
Network signals: HTTP/2 SETTINGS acks delayed on some proxies, causing a buildup of half-open streams and backpressure into apigw accept queue.
Correlated events: autoscaler thaw of ephemeral workers at 02:06 UTC coincides with canary shift. Several runtime nodes showed increased pagefaults and GPU driver soft-resets.
Repro: Non-production replay of same reshuffle at lower QPS reproduced accept-queue growth and small number of runtime NVML timeouts—suggests workload amplification from reshuffle + thaw interaction.
actions_taken: 03/12 02:15 UTC: Pinned Acme AI route to previous stable variant to stop reshuffle traffic (immediate mitigation).
03/12 02:18 UTC: Increased apigw accept-queue capacity for dedicated pool and raised per-tenant connection limits temporarily.
03/12 02:22 UTC: Temporarily disabled aggressive worker thaw policy for the affected autoscaler group.
03/12 02:30 UTC: Eng SRE created a hotfix PR to add an extra backpressure window before variant transition (PR #2356).
workaround: Pinned customer route to last-known-good model variant and disabled canary transitions for that pool; increased apigw accept-queue headroom and throttled canary ramp for scheduled rollouts.
resolution: Mitigation applied: pin and throttle prevented further customer-impacting 5xx waves. Root cause under investigation: combination of reshuffle-driven kernel compilation and HTTP/2 stream accumulation exposed a timing window where NVML timeouts occurred. Action items: land backpressure throttle PR, adjust worker-thaw schedule, add healthcheck gating for variant transitions. Target for permanent fix: 2026-03-20 (pending QA).

Marina Kovács (SRE, 2026-03-12): Pinned route and applied temporary apigw headroom. Observed error rate drop to <1% after mitigation.
Priya Nair (Support, 2026-03-12): Informed Acme AI CS contact about the mitigation and provided ETA for rollback of pin once stable rollout policy is updated.
